newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends lower on ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends lower on ample liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 60 basis points at 18.20 percent on Friday in a market awash with liquidity, traders said.
"The market opened with rates almost unchanged, but liquidity flooded in again before the close," a trader said.
Traders noted that investors often choose to go into money market instruments that accrue interest over the weekend while other markets are closed.
Yields on the overnight Cetes declined 120 basis points from the previous week.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile declined 10 basis points to 19.60 percent.
Benchmark 48-hour contracts ended 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.7500/7.7520 per dollar.

"News like loan prepayment to the IMF, new central bank measures to stabilize the forex market and the outlook for lower inflation in the coming months helped secondary rates to fall over the week," a trader said.
Traders said that improved unemployment figures released in late trade did not affect dealing and that they were instead looking ahead to inflation figures due out on Monday.
Mexican open unemployment in January was 4.5 percent, compared to 6.4 percent for the same month in 1996, the National Statistics Institute said shortly after the close of trade.
Banco de Mexico is expected to release inflation figures for the first half of February on Monday.
A Reuters survey of financial professionals in Mexico City shows they expect consumer prices to rise by an average of 0.88 percent, compared to 0.94 percent for the second half of January.
Dealers said current market liquidity and an optimistic outlook for inflation led to forecasts that primary interest rates could fall once more at next week's central bank auction.
"We expect the inflation data to come in low, and if that's the case then there is some room for primary rates to fall gain," a trader said.
Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates currently stand at 19.46 percent.
"You have to take into account that demand slumped last week, so everything depends on inflation figures," another trader said.
Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity in the market by draining 2.208 billion pesos through four auctions with maturities ranging from three to 23 days.

"Banco de Mexico has been draining liquidity at longer and longer maturities which means there will be no liquidity problems in the short term. They can withdraw money for longer term as there is plenty of funding," a dealer said.
Liquidity of 198 million pesos is expected to return to the market on Monday.
